Fixes #36411.

issue_context.title: The default route of a pppoe interface is removed after restarting systemd-networkd
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

systemd 257.2-2

### Used distribution

Arch Linux

### Linux kernel version used

6.12.10-arch1-1

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

networkctl, systemd-networkd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

The default route of the ppp interface remains unchanged

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

The default route of the ppp interface is removed

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. wait for pppd and systemd-networkd to finish configuring the ppp0 interface
2. run `systemctl restart systemd-networkd`
3. `ip -r` shows the default route is removed

comments:
content of the ppp.network

```
[Match]
Type=ppp

[Network]
IPForward=yes

IPv6AcceptRA=yes

KeepConfiguration=yes

[IPv6AcceptRA]

DHCPv6Client=always
```
`ManageForeignRoutes` default to yes but I have explicitly set `KeepConfiguration=yes`
The similar issue I mentioned before is https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/35094
Is it new in v257? Or reproducible with an older release?

I found some explanation about the "boot" protocol.  [manual of ip-route](https://man.archlinux.org/man/ip-route.8#protocol) and [some blog](https://utcc.utoronto.ca/~cks/space/blog/linux/IpRouteProtoWhat)

The route got removed was added by pppd (the `defaultroute` option) and it has the protocol boot set. According to the manual, route with boot proto will purged by a routing daemon.

So I wonder if networkd was doing the right thing, and maybe pppd should specify some other protocol?

> Is it new in v257? Or reproducible with an older release?

I experienced this route lost about several months ago, but I didn't pay attention to  the version of systemd. I can remember that the route would not be removed when I switched to networkd around 3 years ago.
Ah, this is a regression in dd6d53a8dc58c5e6e310b09ba7f7a22600a87ba9 (v257).

review_comments: Previously this didn't look at `nexthop->protocol` at all, now it does. Is protocol always `RTPROT_STATIC` here? Otherwise this is a behavior change, while the commit message says it's not supposed to be a behavior change.

The nexthops statically configured by networkd has RTPROT_STATIC with NETWORK_CONFIG_SOURCE_STATIC.
When configured dynamically, it has RTPROT_RA or so with NETWORK_CONFIG_SOURCE_NDISC.
Currently, the kernel does not configure any nexthops implicitly.
So, the behavior may be changed only when a user manually configures nexthops.
For neighbor entries, currently we do not set/get/manage protocol field, and the behavior is unchanged.
I will extend the commit message.
